## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pārājika 8, titled *Aṭṭhavatthukā* ("The training rule on behaving inappropriately in eight ways"), is the eighth and final rule entailing expulsion (*pārājika*) for fully ordained nuns in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a nun who consents to all eight forms of flirtatious misconduct with an impassioned man commits an offense of defeat and is expelled from the community [SuttaCentral]. Biblically and structurally, this is the first among a substantial group of rules in the Vinaya whose origin story features the notorious group of six nuns (*chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo*), who were either affiliated with or literary counterparts to the group of six monks [SuttaCentral]. A complete modern English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the rule in the Theravāda *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pj 8) and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Pj 8) [SuttaCentral]. In other Vinaya lineages, the rule corresponds to the sixth *pārājika*, designated either as *Aṭṭhavatthukā* in the Mahāsāṃghika and Lokottaravāda traditions, or under the title *Vajjappaṭicchādikā* in the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, and Mūlasarvāstivāda recensions preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus documents 653 matching segments shared across 72 Pali texts, exhibiting heavy formulaic overlap with the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, related Vibhaṅga provisions (such as Bi-Vb Pj 5, Pj 6, Pj 7, and Ss 5), and later exegetical treatises including the *Pācittiya-aṭṭhakathā*, *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā*, and *Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments in DharmaNexus corroborate correspondences with the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* and the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (Degé D 5) and associated Vinaya commentaries [DharmaNexus].
